action: Organisations that send texts through CSCTelecom: ask what of your traffic was exposed and whether it was accessed. Old one-time codes have expired, but warn customers about scams that reference past messages. No action is needed by most individuals.
date_note: Reported in a Nov 6-12 roundup; exact disclosure day not confirmed
exec: A messaging supplier's exposed database leaked years of one-time codes and sensitive texts; the gap is closed but past exposure remains.
impact: About 125 million text messages were exposed. That is a count of messages, not of people.
plain: A database belonging to telecom firm CSCTelecom was left open, exposing about 125 million text messages sent from October 2022 to September 2026, including bank login codes and emergency-line messages. It has since been secured.
summary: An exposed database leaked SMS messages sent between October 2022 and September 2026, including bank authentication codes and emergency-hotline messages. The exposure has been fixed.
title: CSCTelecom database exposed 125 million SMS messages

validation.note: One roundup; exact disclosure day unknown.
